standard_prerequisites: Integral closed subspaces and their generic points, the closure of the image of a generic point being the generic point of an integral closed subspace, and the reduction of a closed subspace
The cartesian description of the points of the preimage of a closed subspace, and the universal property of the reduction
Stability of properness under composition, under base change and for closed immersions, and closedness of the image of a proper morphism
core_obligations: Take the generic point of the given integral closed subspace, look at its image, and define the candidate image as the integral closed subspace whose generic point is that image

Show that the given subspace is contained in the preimage of that candidate, using the cartesian description of points and the universal property of the reduction, which produces the required morphism
Record that this morphism is dominant because the generic point maps to the generic point, and that the candidate is unique

In the proper case, note that the composite of the given subspace with the morphism is proper as a composition of proper morphisms, deduce properness of the induced morphism by stability under composition, and conclude surjectivity because the image of a proper morphism is closed
proof_roadmap: Define the image through the generic point and construct the morphism from the subspace to it
In the proper case use stability of properness and closedness of the image to obtain properness and surjectivity
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the existence, uniqueness and properness of the dominant image of an integral closed subspace at source lines 819-833, label lemma-proper-image, whose proof occupies source lines 835-854. The construction is driven by the generic point: the image is defined as the integral closed subspace whose generic point is the image of the generic point, and the existence of the morphism is obtained by combining the cartesian description of the points of a preimage with the universal property of the reduction, after which dominance is automatic and uniqueness is clear. The proper case needs a short chain: the composite is proper as a composite of proper morphisms, stability under composition gives properness of the induced morphism, and surjectivity follows because the image of a proper morphism is closed. The counted statement records none of this.
